Detail not fixed by the spec and chosen to fit: collar sizes, drive layout, exact mount and cell positions.
what her embarked fleet takes up, against her own hull
Volume of her hull box (8.8 km³)
embarked hulls 0.33 km³ (3.7%) · their bays and clearances 0.89 km³ (10%)
embarked hulls 0.24 Bt (1.1%) · her own armor and structure 14.2 Bt (65%)
The whole embarked fleet, 64 hulls and 1,146 small craft, fills about a tenth
of her hull box and weighs about a ninetieth of her. A modern aircraft carrier's air
wing is roughly 1–2% of the ship's weight, so the ratio is in the same family.
The reason to carry them is sound.
Only the Iskar has a warp drive. Anything flying alongside is left behind
on every jump and arrives weeks later by cruise, so the escorts have to ride inside.
Not the fleet but the empty space: about two-fifths of her districts stand
sealed, and armor is two-thirds of her mass. The big-number feel comes from her
size, 7.2 km and 22 billion tons, not from how many ships she holds.
Where a reader might push back.
A Casakin is 720 m, a city block's worth of warship in each shaft. Twenty
of them inside one hull is a lot to picture; the dock drawing helps sell it.
